codes.label: UAT power-up code
codes.meaning: Used by certain UAT ADS-B units on power-up until the aircraft enters beacon interrogation coverage. ATC never assigns it.
codes.source: JO 7110.66H, Appendix A, TBL A-1; paragraph 7e

codes.label: ADS-B Mode 3/A inhibit
codes.meaning: Used exclusively by ADS-B aircraft to inhibit Mode 3/A transmission.

codes.label: VFR
codes.meaning: VFR aircraft that may or may not be in contact with ATC.
codes.source: JO 7110.66H, Appendix A, TBL A-1; AIM 4-1-20

codes.label: VFR, Los Angeles SFRA
codes.meaning: VFR aircraft operating in the Los Angeles Special Flight Rules Area.

codes.label: VFR glider
codes.meaning: VFR gliders that may or may not be in contact with ATC.
codes.source: JO 7110.66H, Appendix A, TBL A-1; AIM 4-1-20

codes.label: VFR formation lead
codes.meaning: VFR standard formation flights not in contact with ATC; the lead aircraft squawks 1203 and the others squawk standby.
codes.source: JO 7110.66H, Appendix A, TBL A-1; AIM 4-1-20

codes.label: VFR helicopters (regional)
codes.meaning: VFR helicopters in the Los Angeles region, or VFR departures from Washington DC SFRA fringe airports.

codes.label: VFR public service helicopters (regional)
codes.meaning: Reserved for VFR public service helicopters in the Los Angeles region.

codes.label: VFR pattern work, Washington DC SFRA
codes.meaning: VFR aircraft conducting pattern work at airports in the Washington DC SFRA.

codes.label: Firefighting aircraft
codes.meaning: Firefighting aircraft; those not in contact with ATC may use it en route to, from or within a firefighting area.
codes.source: JO 7110.66H, Appendix A, TBL A-1; AIM 4-1-20

codes.label: Ground test transponders
codes.meaning: Calibration Performance Monitoring Equipment, MSSR Remote System Monitor and PARROT transponders.

codes.label: ADIZ penetration without communication
codes.meaning: Air Defense Identification Zone penetration when unable to establish communication with ATC or an aeronautical facility.

codes.label: Search and rescue
codes.meaning: Designated search and rescue aircraft; VFR aircraft on authorized USAF or USCG SAR missions may be advised to use it.
codes.source: JO 7110.66H, Appendix A, TBL A-1; AIM 4-1-20

codes.label: Military restricted/warning areas
codes.meaning: Military pilots operating within restricted or warning areas use it unless ATC assigns another code. The order also lists 4000 among external ARTCC code blocks.
codes.source: AIM 4-1-20; JO 7110.66H, Appendix A, TBL A-1

codes.label: Reserved subset
codes.meaning: Reserved/allocated subset; the order does not publish its users.

codes.label: Weather reconnaissance
codes.meaning: Weather reconnaissance, as appropriate.

codes.label: Reserved subset
codes.meaning: Reserved/allocated subset; the order does not publish its users.

codes.label: High balloon operations
codes.meaning: High balloon operations by the National Scientific Balloon Facility and other providers, some in international operations.

codes.label: Reserved subset
codes.meaning: Reserved/allocated subset; the order does not publish its users.

codes.label: Unmanned aircraft lost link
codes.meaning: Reserved for an unmanned aircraft experiencing a lost link situation.

codes.label: Unlawful interference
codes.meaning: Hijack/unlawful interference; reserved internationally.

codes.label: Reserved subset
codes.meaning: Reserved/allocated subset; the order does not publish its users.

codes.label: Communication failure
codes.meaning: Communication failure; reserved internationally.

codes.label: Reserved subset
codes.meaning: Reserved/allocated subset; the order does not publish its users.

codes.label: Emergency
codes.meaning: Emergency; reserved internationally.

codes.label: Reserved subset
codes.meaning: Reserved/allocated subset; the order does not publish its users.

codes.label: Military interceptor operations
codes.meaning: Reserved for military interceptor operations; civil aircraft must never use it.
codes.source: AIM 4-1-20; JO 7110.66H, Appendix A, TBL A-1 (reserved/allocated)

jurisdiction: US domestic, oceanic and arctic airspace (FAA)
notes: United States allocations. Other States allocate codes differently, facilities can reuse codes locally, and a code alone never establishes a mission, an emergency or the aircraft's operator.
Sensitive entries are reserved subsets whose users are not published; public text must not speculate about them.
